theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

A price list says "J$450 ea". What does "ea" mean?

Bolts come in boxes of 50. You need 120 bolts. How many boxes should you order?
What do we call goods that are sent back to the supplier because they are wrong or damaged?

essays.stem: Describe how you would work out exactly what materials to order for a job.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the drawing, the job sheet or the cutting list, and read the notes for the material, sizes and finish. I make a list of every item, with its full description and the quantity needed, including fixings and consumables such as electrodes, grinding discs, paint, screws or cable ties. I add up the lengths or quantities and change them into the units the supplier sells, such as 6 m lengths, 100 m rolls or boxes of 50, always rounding up, and I add a small allowance for cutting and waste. Then I check the store and the site to see what we already have, and take this away from the list, so that only what is needed is ordered. I check when the materials are needed, so that the order can be placed in time. Finally I ask my supervisor to check the list.
markingPoints: Uses the drawing, job sheet or cutting list
Lists every item with full description and quantity, including fixings and consumables
Converts to supplier units, rounds up and allows for waste
Checks existing stock and orders only what is needed
Checks when materials are needed and has the list checked

essays.stem: Explain why an order must give a full description of each item, and give examples of the details needed for steel and for electrical items.
essays.modelAnswer: A supplier sells many sizes and types of each item, so a vague order such as "some flat bar" or "cable" can bring the wrong goods. Wrong goods waste time, hold up the job and cost money to return, and the wrong material may even be unsafe. A full description makes sure that the right item, in the right amount, arrives the first time. For steel, I give the type of section, such as flat bar, angle, square tube or plate; the size and thickness, such as 40 mm × 5 mm flat bar or 25 mm square tube with 1.5 mm wall; the length or sheet size; the grade or finish, such as mild steel or galvanised; and the number of pieces. For electrical items, I give the type, the size and the rating, such as the cable type and size or a socket outlet's type and current rating, the colour where it matters, and the number or length needed.
markingPoints: Suppliers sell many sizes and types, so vague orders bring wrong goods
Wrong goods cause delay, cost and possible safety problems
Steel: section type, size and thickness, length, grade or finish, quantity
Electrical: type, size, rating, colour where needed, quantity or length
The right goods arrive first time

essays.stem: Explain how you would choose a supplier for an order of materials.
essays.modelAnswer: I first look at the business's list of approved suppliers, because these have already been checked for reliability and quality. I ask two or three of them for a price for exactly the same items, so that I can compare them fairly. I compare more than the price. I check the quality, for example whether the steel is the right grade and not rusty, or whether the electrical fittings are of a safe, approved type. I check whether they have the items in stock and how long they take to deliver, because a cheap price is no good if the goods arrive after the job should start. I also think about delivery charges, payment terms, how they handled past problems and returns, and whether they can deliver to the site. Then I choose the best value, not just the cheapest, and get my supervisor's approval.
markingPoints: Uses the approved supplier list
Gets prices for the same items from more than one supplier
Compares quality and safety, not just price
Compares stock, delivery time, delivery cost and payment terms
Chooses best value and gets approval

essays.stem: Describe the steps from finding that materials are needed to the order being placed with the supplier.
essays.modelAnswer: When I find that materials are needed, I first check the store and the stock records to see what we already have. For the items we do not have, I fill in a purchase requisition with a full description of each item, the quantity, the job number and the date they are needed. I give it to my supervisor or the person who is allowed to approve spending. Once it is approved, a purchase order is made out to the chosen supplier, with an order number, the supplier's name, each item with its description, quantity and price, the delivery address and date, and the signature of the authorised person. The order is sent by email, by phone or in person. If it is placed by phone, it is confirmed in writing. I check the supplier's confirmation for the items, prices and delivery date, and file copies of all the papers.
markingPoints: Checks existing stock first
Completes a purchase requisition with full details and the date needed
Gets approval from an authorised person
Purchase order with number, items, quantities, prices, delivery details and signature
Places the order, confirms it, checks the confirmation and files the papers

essays.stem: Describe how you would receive and check a delivery of materials.
essays.modelAnswer: I make sure there is a clear, safe area to unload and that I have the purchase order to hand. I wear gloves and safety boots, and get help or lifting equipment for heavy or long items. Before I sign anything, I check the goods against the delivery note and the purchase order. I count every item and check the descriptions, sizes and grades, using a tape or vernier caliper where needed, for example the thickness of plate or the size of cable. I look for damage, rust, bent lengths, broken fittings or wet packets. If everything is correct, I sign and date the delivery note and keep a copy. If anything is wrong, I write it clearly on the delivery note before signing and tell my supervisor. Then I fill in the goods received note, update the stock records and store the materials in the right place.
markingPoints: Prepares a safe unloading area and wears PPE; safe lifting
Checks against the delivery note and the purchase order before signing
Counts and checks sizes, grades and condition
Signs only when correct, or records problems on the note and reports them
Completes the goods received note, updates stock records and stores the goods

essays.stem: Explain what you would do if a delivery is short, damaged or not what was ordered.
essays.modelAnswer: I do not just accept it or throw anything away. I write exactly what is wrong on the delivery note before I sign it, for example "8 lengths received, 10 ordered" or "2 light fittings broken", and ask the driver to sign or note it too if possible. I take photos of any damage. I keep the wrong or damaged goods separate, labelled and safe, and do not use them. I tell my supervisor straight away, because the job may be held up. Then the supplier is contacted the same day, by phone and in writing, giving the order number and the details, and asked to send the missing or correct items and collect the wrong ones. The goods received note shows what really arrived, so that the business only pays for good items. A credit note should be received for anything returned, and I file all the papers together.
markingPoints: Records the problem on the delivery note before signing, with photos of damage
Keeps wrong or damaged goods separate and does not use them
Tells the supervisor quickly
Contacts the supplier with the order number, in writing, to replace or collect
Records what actually arrived; gets a credit note; files the papers

essays.stem: Describe how to store steel, welding electrodes, gas cylinders, electrical cable and paints safely and in good condition.
essays.modelAnswer: Steel bars, tube and plate are stored on strong racks off the floor, sorted and labelled by size, under cover to keep off rain, with long lengths not sticking out into walkways. Plate is stacked flat or stored in a sheet rack. Welding electrodes are kept dry and sealed in their packets, in a dry store or electrode oven as the maker's instructions say, because damp electrodes give poor welds. Gas cylinders are stored upright and chained, in a well-ventilated area away from heat, with valves closed and caps on, oxygen kept apart from fuel gases, and full and empty cylinders kept separate. Cable rolls and drums are kept dry, off the floor and labelled with their size and type. Paints, thinners and solvents are kept in their labelled containers with lids tight, in a ventilated store away from sparks and heat, with a fire extinguisher nearby.
markingPoints: Steel: racks off the floor, sorted, labelled, under cover, out of walkways
Electrodes: dry and sealed, as the maker's instructions say
Gas cylinders: upright, chained, ventilated, away from heat, oxygen apart from fuel gas
Cable: dry, off the floor, labelled
Paints and solvents: labelled, lids on, ventilated store, away from sparks, extinguisher nearby

essays.stem: Explain how a simple stock control system works in a workshop store, and why it is useful.
essays.modelAnswer: Each item in the store has its own place and a bin card or a line in a computer stock list. Every time items come in or go out, the card is filled in with the date, the quantity, who took it or which delivery it came from, and the new balance. This means anyone can see how much is in stock. Each item has a reorder level: when the balance falls to that level, more is ordered, so the store does not run out while waiting for the lead time. A small buffer stock may be kept in case a delivery is late. Older stock is used first, which is called first in, first out, so that materials such as electrodes and paint do not go out of date. From time to time a stocktake is done to count everything and correct the records. This saves money, stops waste and theft, and keeps jobs running.
markingPoints: Each item has a place and a bin card or computer record
Every movement in and out is recorded with the new balance
Reorder level and buffer stock prevent running out
First in, first out stops old stock going out of date
Stocktakes correct the records; saves money and keeps jobs running

essays.stem: Describe how to unload and move heavy or long materials, such as steel lengths, plate and cable drums, safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I plan the move first: I check the weight and length, clear the route and the place where the materials will go, and make sure the ground is firm and dry. I wear gloves to protect my hands from sharp edges and burrs, and safety boots in case something drops. For heavy items I use lifting aids, such as a trolley, a forklift operated by a trained person, or a hoist, instead of lifting by hand. If I must lift by hand, I bend my knees, keep my back straight, hold the load close to my body and do not twist. Long lengths of steel are carried by two people, one at each end, who talk to each other and move together, taking care at corners and doorways. Cable drums are rolled carefully in the direction shown on the drum, or lifted with a proper drum stand. I never throw materials off a truck or stand under a load.
markingPoints: Plans the move: weight, route and destination clear
Wears gloves and safety boots
Uses lifting aids, with trained operators where needed
Safe lifting posture; two-person carry for long lengths with clear communication
Never throws materials or stands under a load; moves drums correctly

essays.stem: Explain how the documents used when ordering materials link together, and why they must be accurate and kept.
essays.modelAnswer: The purchase requisition is the internal request that says what is needed and why. When it is approved, a purchase order is sent to the supplier, with its own number, saying exactly what is being bought and at what price. When the goods arrive, they come with a delivery note from the supplier listing what was sent. The business checks the goods and records what actually arrived on a goods received note. The supplier then sends an invoice asking for payment. Before it is paid, the invoice is matched with the purchase order and the goods received note, so that the business only pays for what it ordered and received, at the agreed price. If goods are returned or overcharged, the supplier sends a credit note. The papers must be accurate and filed together under the order number, so that any problem can be traced and the accounts are correct.
markingPoints: Requisition: internal request, approved
Purchase order: sent to the supplier with number, items and prices
Delivery note and goods received note: what was sent and what actually arrived
Invoice matched to the order and goods received before payment; credit note for returns
Accurate, filed together so that problems can be traced and accounts are correct

practical1.title: Prepare a materials list, requisition and purchase order for a job
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a drawing and job sheet, for example for a welded steel workbench frame or for the wiring of a small workshop room. As a group, work out exactly what must be ordered. Make a full materials list with descriptions, sizes and quantities, including fixings and consumables, and change the quantities into the units the supplier sells. Check the Centre's store for any items already in stock and record what you find. Compare the prices of the remaining items on two or three supplier price lists given by the assessor, and choose the best value. Complete a purchase requisition, get it approved by your "supervisor" (the assessor), then complete a purchase order. Finally, one member places the order by phone in a role play with the assessor as the supplier, while another records the order number and the delivery date. Share the work so that every member completes and checks a part. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: The drawing and job sheet from the assessor
Two or three supplier price lists
Blank materials list, stock check sheet, comparison table, purchase requisition and purchase order forms
Access to the Centre's store and its stock cards (with the storekeeper's permission)
Safety boots and gloves for the store
photos: The group reading the drawing and starting the materials list
The finished materials list with full descriptions and quantities
Members checking stock in the store, with the stock check sheet
The price comparison table with the chosen supplier marked
The approved purchase requisition and the completed purchase order
The phone order role play, with the order number recorded
checklist: Read the drawing correctly and listed every item needed
Gave a full description of each item (type, size, grade or rating, quantity)
Changed quantities into supplier units, rounding up and allowing for waste
Checked the store and recorded the stock found accurately
Compared suppliers on price, quality and delivery, and chose best value
Completed the requisition and purchase order fully and correctly
Placed or recorded the phone order clearly, with the order number and delivery date
Checked another member's work and corrected any mistake
safety: Enter the store only with the storekeeper's or assessor's permission
Wear safety boots and gloves in the store; watch for sharp edges on steel
Do not climb racks or pull out long lengths; look and count only
Do not move gas cylinders or open containers of paint or chemicals

practical2.title: Receive, check and store a delivery, and update the stock records
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a "delivery" from the Centre's store, with a purchase order and a delivery note. The delivery has some mistakes in it, such as a short quantity, a wrong size and a damaged item. As a group, prepare a safe unloading area, then check every item against the purchase order and the delivery note, counting and measuring with a tape and a vernier caliper. Record every problem on the delivery note before "signing" it, and photograph any damage. Complete a goods received note, and write a short message to the supplier listing the problems with the order number. Then store the correct items in the right places, using safe lifting and two-person carries for long lengths, keep the wrong or damaged items separate and labelled, and update the bin cards. Share the work so that every member checks some items, helps to store them and fills in part of the paperwork. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A set-up delivery of materials from the Centre's store (for example steel lengths, plate offcuts, electrode packets, cable rolls, fittings)
The purchase order and the delivery note from the assessor
Goods received note forms and bin cards
Labels, markers and a phone or tablet for photos
Gloves, safety boots and a trolley
photos: The unloading area cleared and the delivery laid out
Members counting and measuring the items, with the paperwork
Each problem found, with the label or note beside it
The delivery note marked with the problems, and the completed goods received note
The materials stored correctly on racks or shelves, with wrong items set apart and labelled
The updated bin cards and the message to the supplier
checklist: Helped prepare a clear, safe area before unloading
Checked items against both the purchase order and the delivery note
Counted and measured accurately, using the tape and vernier caliper correctly
Found and recorded the mistakes before the delivery note was signed
Completed the goods received note and updated the bin cards correctly
Wrote a clear message to the supplier with the order number and the problems
Lifted and carried safely, using two people for long lengths
Stored each item in the right place and kept wrong or damaged items separate
safety: Wear gloves and safety boots throughout
Use two people for long lengths and a trolley for heavy items; bend your knees and keep your back straight
Keep walkways clear; do not leave lengths sticking out from racks
Do not climb racks; put heavy items on the lower shelves
Do not open or move gas cylinders during this task
